results.submittedClaim: No contraindications stated in either pre-1900 source; record as 'not stated classically', not as 'none'.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: The claim names NO sources at all ('either pre-1900 source'), so as written it cannot be checked. I checked the two obvious candidates myself. (1) Dutt, Materia Medica of the Hindus (1877): there is NO standalone monograph for Withania somnifera. It appears only as a compound ingredient (e.g. 'Kasisadyataila... wood of Withania somnifera (asvagandha)', p.55; 'Masha baladi kvatha', p.121; 'Narayana taila', p.261; 'Lakshaditaila', p.277; 'Chhagaladya ghrita', p.238) and in King's glossary ('Asvagandha ... Withania somnifera, Don. Syn. Physalis flexuosa, Roxb.'). No contraindication. (2) Dymock, Warden & Hooper, Pharmacographia Indica vol. II (1890), pp. 566-568, WITHANIA SOMNIFERA, Dunal: DOES carry a safety statement, under the heading 'Toxicology' — 'Dr. Burton Brown (Punjab Poisons) records a fatal case of poisoning by the seeds of this plant. The symptoms observed were vomiting, insensibility, convulsions; the patient became unconscious with dilated pupils insensible to light; there were continued tetanic spasms of the muscles of the face and extremities...'. That is seed toxicology, not a formal contraindication for the root, but it is not 'nothing'. The conservative recording instruction ('not stated classically', not 'none') is sound and should be kept; the blanket assertion of silence is overstated for Dymock.

results.submittedClaim: HONEST GAP — no contraindication in BCGM 1596 or Bhavaprakasha; do not manufacture one; the 三稜 caution 能瀉真氣真氣虚者勿用 belongs to San Leng and must not be carried across.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: The 三稜 half is exactly right and important: BCGM 卷十四, 荆三稜 氣味 note, sits immediately before the 莎草香附子 entry and reads 「元素曰苦甘無毒隂中之陽能瀉真氣真氣虚者勿用」 — Zhang Yuansu, on San Leng, not Xiang Fu. The 'no contraindication at all' half OVERSTATES. BCGM 卷十四 發明 carries 好古's caution 「炒黒能止血治崩漏此婦人之仙藥也多服亦能走氣」 (taken in quantity it also scatters qi), and 本草從新 1757 carries an explicit patient restriction: 「苦燥而能耗血散氣。（士材曰：乃治標之品、唯氣實血未大虚者宜之、不然、恐損氣而耗血、愈致其疾矣…）」 — suitable only where qi is replete and blood not greatly depleted. Both are pre-1900 and both were missed. The Bhavaprakasha half is UNVERIFIED: I had no access to a pre-1900 Sanskrit text of the Nighantu and did not confirm or refute it.
results.sourceAndYear: 本草綱目 (1596) 卷十四; 本草從新 (吳儀洛), 1757

results.submittedClaim: Wu Yiluo 1757 「入肝腎」 is the EARLIEST clean pre-1900 warrant for Liver/Kidney; a second, different pre-1900 reading is Wang Ang 1694 quoting Shizhen as 手足陽明、三焦、命門藥 — 'two pre-1900 channel maps, not one'.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: Both quotations are real, but the priority and the 'two competing works' framing are wrong. 本草備要 1694 (Wang Ang), 淫羊藿, reads: 「辛香甘温。入肝肾。补命门（时珍曰∶手足阳明、三焦、命门药），益精气，坚筋骨，利小便。」 — the Liver/Kidney assignment AND the Shizhen Yangming/Sanjiao/Mingmen line sit side by side in the SAME 1694 entry, 63 years before Wu Yiluo. So 1757 is not the earliest warrant for 入肝腎, and the two readings are not rival sources but complementary lines in one entry. 本草從新 1757 does read 「辛香甘溫。入肝腎。補命門。」 as claimed. The Shizhen line traces further back still, verbatim in BCGM 1596 卷十二下 發明: 「時珍曰滛羊藿味甘氣香性温不寒能益精氣乃手足陽明三焦命門藥也真陽不足者宜之」.

results.herb: Green Tea (茗 / 茶, Camellia sinensis)
results.submittedClaim: No Shennong grade — tea is not in the Shennong Bencao Jing. BCGM tags 茗 as 「唐本草」 with 「校正…自木部移入此」. Sun Xingyan 1799 mentions 茗 only inside the 苦菜 entry's philological note, where Tao Hongjing identified 苦菜 with tea and the Tang commentary rejected it: 「《唐本》注駁之，非矣」.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: BCGM 卷32 (果部): 「{{SK anchor|茗}}{{SK notes|唐本草}}　校正{{SK notes|自木部移入此}}」 — verbatim. Shennong Bencao Jing (Sun Xingyan 1799): no 茗 or 茶 entry exists in any of the three juan; the only occurrence of 茗 is at line 1380, inside the 案 note appended to 苦菜 (卷一·上經): 「郭璞云…今呼早萊者為荼，晚取者為茗…陶弘景云：此即是今茗，茗，一名荼，又令人不眠…生益州。《唐本》注駁之，非矣。」 Substantively correct. Two refinements worth carrying: (a) 非矣 is Sun Xingyan's own verdict that the Tang refutation was mistaken, i.e. he leans toward Tao Hongjing's identification — so the note is not a clean 'tea is out'; (b) 苦菜 itself IS an upper-grade entry (卷一, 「久服，安心益氣，聰察少臥，輕身、耐老」), which is presumably where any 'upper grade tea' claim originates. The claim's operative conclusion — that no Han-dynasty duration ruling exists for 茗 as such — holds.

results.whatSourceActuallySays: The absence is confirmed, but the identity underlying it is not what the row assumes, and that is the more serious finding. Neither pre-1900 source identifies Shankhapushpi as Convolvulus pluricaulis — the string 'pluricaulis' does not occur once in any of the three volumes of Pharmacographia Indica. Dutt 1877 pp. 201-202 heads the entry "CANSCORA DECUSSATA, R. et Sch. … Sans. Sankhapushpi. Vern. Dankuni, Beng. Sankhahuli, Hind." and describes it as "laxative, alterative and tonic and … much praised as a nervine," used in insanity, epilepsy and nervous debility — no contraindication. Dymock Vol. II, under XANTHIUM STRUMARIUM, Linn., says the plant "is said to be the Shankhini or Shankhapushpi of Sanskrit writers" — and that entry DOES carry a toxicity remark: "In America and Australia this plant has been observed to prove fatal to cattle and pigs which have pastured upon it." That is a Xanthium note, not a Convolvulus note, and is livestock-specific. So: no contraindication for the herb as the row defines it, plus a botanical-identity conflict the claim does not flag.

results.whatSourceActuallySays: The 1596 half is fully verified. BCGM 卷17下: 「之才曰射干為之使惡皂莢畏雄黄生薑乾薑秦皮{{SKchar|1841}}甲反烏頭權曰柴胡為之使忌羊血海{{SKchar|3610}}飴糖元素曰熱痰佐以黄芩…多用則㵼脾胃諸血證及口渇者禁用為其燥津液也孕婦忌之用生薑則無害」. 別錄 墮胎 confirmed in both witnesses. THE ZHENGLEI CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD AS FRAMED. 證類本草 (Siku/WYG recension) 卷10 does read 「射干為之使惡皂莢畏雄黄生薑乾薑秦皮龜甲及烏頭」 — 及, as claimed. But 重修政和證類本草 (Sibu Congkan recension) 卷10 reads 「射干爲之使惡皂莢畏雄黄生薑乾薑秦皮龜甲反烏頭」 — 反烏頭, identical to BCGM. So this is a variant BETWEEN Zhenglei recensions, not a doctrinal divergence between 1108 and 1596, and recording it as the latter would put a false textual-history statement into the database. Two smaller slips: the harvester silently normalised 龜甲 and 海藻 from lacuna glyphs ({{SKchar|1841}}, {{SKchar|3610}}) without flagging them, unlike its own careful flag on the Reishi claim; and its ellipsis elides 元素曰, so the 多用則㵼脾胃 / 孕婦忌之 material reads as anonymous BCGM text when the source attributes it to Zhang Yuansu.

results.submittedClaim: Not in the Shennong Bencao Jing; BCGM heads it 「宋開寳」, first entering the Chinese record in the Kaibao Bencao (973 CE). Bhavaprakasha 2.207 classes it रसायनी and Dymock 1890 confirms 'The Hindus class them with the rasāyāna or alchemic drugs.'
results.whatSourceActuallySays: Absence confirmed: neither 補骨脂 nor 破故紙 occurs anywhere in the Sun Xingyan 1799 recension (zero hits across all three juan). BCGM 卷14: 「{{SK anchor|補骨脂}}{{SK notes|宋開寳}}」 — the 宋開寳 head tag is exact, and the 集解 opens 「志曰補骨脂生嶺南諸州及波斯國」 (Ma Zhi, the Kaibao compiler), confirming Song-Kaibao first entry as a foreign import. One citation slip: the Bhavaprakasha locus is not 2.207. In the Vargaprakaraṇa, Harītakyādivarga, verse 208 gives the synonyms 「avalgujo vākucī syāt somarājī suparṇikā…」 and verse 209 carries the classification 「vākucī madhurā tiktā kaṭupākā rasāyanī」; verse 207 is the tail of the unrelated rasāñjana entry. Substance right, verse and section number wrong.

results.submittedClaim: Wu Yiluo 1757 「破故紙 一名補骨脂。燥補命火。辛苦大溫。入心包命門。補相火以通君火。」; Li Shizhen 1596 gives the same mechanism in the 發明: 「破故紙屬火收歛神明能使心包之火與命門之火相通故元陽堅固骨髓充實」.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: The 1757 half is verbatim. 本草從新: 「破故紙 一名補骨脂。燥補命火。辛苦大溫。入心包命門。補相火以通君火。暖丹田。壮元陽。」 — exact. The 1596 half quotes the right characters but the wrong speaker. BCGM 卷14 發明 reads 「時珍曰…按白飛霞方外竒方云破故紙屬火收歛神明能使心包之火與命門之火相通故元陽堅固骨髓充實濇以治脫也」 — Li Shizhen is expressly citing Bai (elsewhere Han) Feixia's 方外奇方, not asserting it in his own voice. 本草從新 attributes the same doctrine to 韓飛霞: 「韩飛霞曰：故紙屬火、堅固元陽…」. The channel pair 心包/命門 stands on the 1757 text; the 1596 line should be credited to Feixia as quoted by Li Shizhen.

results.submittedClaim: (1) 「墮胎」 = CAUSES MISCARRIAGE, from the 開寳 line 「及婦人血氣墮胎」 in BCGM and repeated by Wu Yiluo; (2) Wu Yiluo 「陰虛有熱。大便闭结者戒之。」; (3) 「珣曰惡甘草」 and 「時珍曰忌芸薹及諸血得胡桃胡麻良」, repeated in the Zheng Xiangguo case as 「忌羊血芸苔」.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: Points (2) and (3) verify. 本草從新: 「陰虚有熱。大便闭结者戒之。」 verbatim; BCGM 卷14 氣味: 「權曰苦辛珣曰惡甘草時珍曰忌芸薹及諸血得胡桃胡麻良」 verbatim, with 珣 = Li Xun and 時珍 = Li Shizhen both correct. Point (1) is REFUTED as read. BCGM's line is 「主治五勞七傷風虚冷骨髓傷敗腎冷精流及婦人血氣墮胎{{SK notes|開寳}}」 — that is the 主治 (indications) field, so 墮胎 is a condition the drug is given FOR, not an adverse effect it produces. 本草從新 makes this explicit by glossing the neighbouring term: 「妇人血氣。（妇人之血脱氣陷、亦犹男子之腎冷精流。）堕胎。陰虚有熱。大便闭结者戒之。」 — 墮胎 sits in the run of treated conditions and the withhold clause (戒之) begins only at 陰虛有熱. Neither pre-1900 text describes 補骨脂 as abortifacient. Also a sourcing slip in (3): the string 「忌羊血芸苔」 is verbatim in 本草從新 1757's version of the Zheng Xiangguo formula, not in BCGM 1596, which reads 「但禁芸薹羊血餘無所忌」.

results.submittedClaim: Wang Haogu 「入手太隂血分」; Zhang Yuansu 「入手少陽陽明經」; Li Shizhen 「黄芩能入手少隂陽明手足太隂少陽六經矣」; Wu Yiluo 1757 「黃芩亦少陽藥也」.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: Three of four are exact. BCGM juan 13 氣味 note: 「好古曰氣寒味㣲苦而甘隂中㣲陽入手太隂血分元素曰氣凉味苦甘氣厚味薄浮而升陽中隂也入手少陽陽明經酒炒則上行」 — Wang Haogu and Zhang Yuansu attributions both correct and verbatim. results.submittedClaim: Li Shizhen 「若因飲寒受寒腹中痛及飲水心下悸小便不利而脉不數者是裏無熱證則黄芩不可用也」; Zhu Zhenheng 「若肺虛者多用則傷肺必先以天門冬保定肺氣而後用之」; Wu Yiluo 「苦寒傷胃。虚寒者。均宜戒。胎前若非實熱而服之。陰損胎元矣。」

results.submittedClaim: (1) Abortifacient — Dymock 1891 on Shitaraj: "...it also causes abortion"; Dutt 1877 p.187 on P. rosea: "The root of Plumbago rosea taken internally will expel the foetus from the womb, whether dead or alive." (2) Caustic/vesicant, with a 15-to-20-minute maximum contact time as a hard classical safety limit. (3) Deliberate abuse by mendicants to raise sores.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: All three quotations are verbatim accurate and correctly attributed; one interpretive gloss is not. Dymock, Pharmacographia Indica vol. II, PLUMBAGINEAE, p.330: "Mahometan writers treat of the drug under the name of Shitaraj... they describe it as caustic and vesicant, an expellant of phlegmatic humors; useful in rheumatism and spleen, digestive; it also causes abortion." Same page: "Such a paste may be applied externally in leprosy and other skin diseases of an obstinate character, and be allowed to remain until a blister has formed. In rheumatism it should be removed after 15 to 20 minutes." Same page: "Religious mendicants attending fairs use the root for the purpose of raising sores upon their bodies, in order to obtain pity and alms." Dutt, p.187: "The root of Plumbago rosea taken internally will expel the foetus from the womb, whether dead or alive" — page number confirmed by the running head on the same page. DETAIL OFF: the "15 to 20 minutes" is NOT a maximum contact time for the drug generally; it is the removal instruction FOR RHEUMATISM ONLY, and the sentence immediately before it prescribes the opposite for skin disease (leave on "until a blister has formed"). Loading it as a universal safety ceiling would invert the source. TWO further items the claim omits and that belong in any safety field: Dymock p.331, "Given internally in large doses, Plumbago root acts as a narcotico-irritant poison", and p.332-region, Madras poisoning statistics including a homicidal case. Also note Dymock treats P. zeylanica and P. rosea in one joint entry and states the Shitaraj material "must be considered to refer to the genus Plumbago, and not to any particular species" — the claim does flag the species distinction, correctly.

results.submittedClaim: 大明 in BCGM lists 「催生墮胎」; Wu Yiluo 1757 repeats 「催生堕胎」; and 'Dutt 1877's own formulary uses it that way', quoting 「Take of the entire plant of Tribulus terrestris… in painful micturition, suppression of urine, bloody urine」 alongside a Sanskrit prescription pairing gokshura with vacha for 催生下衣 equivalents.
results.whatSourceActuallySays: The Chinese half is sound. BCGM 卷十六 主治: 「治奔豚腎氣肺氣胸膈滿催生墮胎益精療水藏冷小便多止遺瀝泄精溺血腫痛{{SK notes|大明}}」 — 催生墮胎 is indeed 大明's. BCGM 附方: 「催生下衣{{SK notes|難産胎在腹中并包衣不下及胎死者蒺䔧子貝母各四兩為末米湯服三錢少頃不下再服　梅師方}}」 — matches. 本草從新 刺蒺藜: 「催生堕胎」; 本草備要 蒺藜子: 「催生堕胎（刺蒺藜主恶血，故能破症下胎）」. The Dutt half is misrepresented. Dutt's Tribulus terrestris entry (pp.125-126) says only: 'They are regarded as cooling, diuretic, tonic and aphrodisiac and are used in painful micturition, calculous affections, urinary disorders and impotence.' The quoted line is real but belongs to Gokshurádya avaleha: 'It is given in doses of two tolas, in painful micturition, suppression of urine, bloody urine, calculous affections etc.' — a urinary electuary of gokshura, ginger, long pepper, black pepper, cinnamon, cardamoms, Mesua ferrea, tejapatra, nutmeg, Terminalia Arjuna and cucumber seeds. There is no vacha in it, no gokshura+vacha labour prescription anywhere in Dutt, and no mention of abortion, miscarriage or parturition in Dutt's Tribulus entry at all. A real quotation has been repurposed to corroborate a claim its source does not make.

## 2. THE REJECT LIST

### The headline "zero REFUTED" is misleading, and this is the most important thing in the report

The tally reports no REFUTED claims. That is true at the claim level and false at the level of what would actually get written. Two PARTLY_VERIFIED claims contain components the verifiers refuted outright, in their own words. If a loader treats PARTLY as "mostly fine, load the good parts", both of these ship.

**H296 Bakuchi, classical_contraindications. The harvest read an indication as an adverse effect and would have printed the inversion as a safety warning.** The claim says 墮胎 in BCGM 卷14 means Bakuchi causes miscarriage. The line is 「主治五勞七傷…及婦人血氣墮胎{{開寳}}」, and that is the 主治 field. 墮胎 there is a condition being treated, not an effect being caused. The verifier's word is REFUTED. This is the single most dangerous item in the batch: a pregnancy-safety statement generated by misreading the direction of a classical sentence, on an herb that is in fact traditionally used in pregnancy-adjacent contexts. It must not ship in any form. The rest of that claim (陰虛有熱、大便闭结者戒之; 惡甘草; 忌芸薹及諸血) verified and can be loaded separately.

**H184 Fu Ling, channel_entry. An author was credited with a doctrine he explicitly rejected.** The claim attributes 白補赤瀉 (white supplements, red drains) to Zhang Yuansu. BCGM 卷37 records 「元素曰伏苓赤瀉白補上古無此説」, which is Zhang Yuansu saying the distinction has no ancient warrant. He disputes it. Separately, the 丙丁/壬癸 split the claim assigns to him is Li Gao's, and the originator named in the source is Tao Hongjing. REFUTED twice over, in the verifier's phrase. The Li Shizhen half of that claim (赤入血分，白入氣分，不當以丙丁壬癸分也) is exact and can be loaded on its own.

### A wrong drug substituted into an incompatibility list

**H184 Fu Ling, classical_contraindications.** The submitted 畏 list ends 鱉甲 (soft-shelled turtle shell). The source reads 龜甲 (tortoise plastron). Different drug, different material, and this is an incompatibility field, so it directly drives formula-blocking logic. Three of the four items in that claim verified verbatim; this one did not. Reject the row, reload with 龜甲.

### Three rows where the harvester filed content into the wrong field

These are pipeline defects, not source defects, and they are quiet enough to slip through a spot-check:

- **H160 Green Tea, channel_entry:** the content under the channel tag is a character-for-character duplicate of the herb's contraindications claim. Nothing in it belongs in a 歸經 field.
- **H284 Water Plantain, classical_contraindications:** the content is a verbatim copy of the herb's grade paragraph (上品, the BCGM head note, the 1799 roster, 久服). It contains no contraindication.
- **H175 Chen Pi, classical_contraindications:** same shape, the grade paragraph pasted under a CONTRA tag.

In all three the pasted text is true. That is exactly why it is dangerous. A reviewer glancing at it sees verified classical Chinese and waves it through, and the live database ends up telling a customer that a contraindication for Chen Pi is that it is an upper-grade herb suitable for long life. Reject all three. Fix the tagger before the next harvest, not after.

### A precise-looking citation that is wrong

**H162 Moringa, classical_contraindications.** The quoted sentence from Dymock is verbatim. The page citation, Vol. I p. 897, is wrong; the entry is at pp. 396 to 398. And the source speaks only to the bark, while the database row extends the pregnancy caution to root and flower. A confident page number attached to real text is the tell that matters here, because it is the thing nobody re-checks. Reject, reload with the correct page and with the caution scoped to bark only.

### A botanical identity that the sources do not support

**H238 Shankhpushpi.** The absence of a contraindication is confirmed, but the verifier found something worse underneath. Neither pre-1900 source identifies Shankhapushpi as *Convolvulus pluricaulis*. The string "pluricaulis" does not appear once in any of the three volumes of Pharmacographia Indica, and Dymock's discussion of the Sanskrit name sits in the *Xanthium strumarium* entry. The row's botanical identity is unsupported. This is not a contraindication problem, it is a "what plant is in the bottle" problem, and it should be escalated out of this workstream.

## 3. The failure rate and its shape

Across the whole reported set, 32 of 254 claims failed to fully verify, which is 12.6 percent. Nothing was refuted at claim level, nothing was unreachable, and no verifier found an invented quotation. Every Chinese quotation checked was a real substring of the named work, in the named juan, under a named authority.

The shape is much more useful than the number, and it is very sharp:

**By field, in the 26 failures I can see:**

- **shennong_grade: 1 failure in 73 claims, 1.4 percent.** And that one (H206) has the correct grade value; only the supporting quote is misattributed. Grade harvesting is effectively solved. It is a single closed enum read off a printed head line, and the harvester gets it right.
- **channel_entry: 13 of 15 visible failures, roughly 18 percent of the field.**
- **classical_contraindications: 12 of 16 visible failures, roughly 17 percent of the field.**

So the failures cluster almost entirely in the two free-text fields, and they cluster for the same underlying reason: those fields require judgment about who said something, in which section of the entry, about which part of the plant, and whether a sentence is an indication or a warning. The grade field requires none of that.

**By kind of error, which is where the money is:**

1. **Attribution errors, 6 instances.** H134 (Li Gao read as Wang Haogu), H274 (Li Shizhen's verdict given to Lei Xiao), H296 (Bai Feixia's line given to Li Shizhen), H294 (Wu Rui's line given to the general voice), H184 (a doctrine given to the man who rejected it), H206 (別錄 given to 本經). Every quotation was real. Every speaker was wrong. This is now the dominant failure mode of the pipeline.
2. **Overstated absence, 4 instances.** H001, H153, H199, H180. Absence claims fail far more often than presence claims because the harvester stops searching once it has enough to say "nothing there". Note that the presence claims verified at close to 100 percent while the absence claims did not.
3. **Field-position errors, 2 instances.** H296 (an indication read as an adverse effect) and, less severely, the H187/H276/H257 dietary lines carried under contraindications. The harvester is not reliably tracking which section of a BCGM entry it is reading.
4. **Field mis-tagging, 3 instances.** H160, H284, H175. Pure pipeline bug: a paragraph pasted under the wrong field name.
5. **Framing and priority errors, 3 instances.** H227, H265, H183. Real text, wrong story about what the text means historically.
6. **Detail substitutions, 3 instances.** H184 (鱉甲 for 龜甲), H104 (an inserted 忌), H162 (a wrong page number). Small, silent, and each one changes meaning.

**By tradition:** the Indian-source claims (Dutt, Dymock, Bhavaprakasha) are a much smaller slice and they carry a different, and arguably worse, problem. Of the eight or so Indian-source claims visible, three are compromised: H162 (wrong page, over-scoped part), H238 (wrong botanical identity), H001 (unnamed sources plus a missed toxicology paragraph), and one, the Bhavaprakasha half of H153, was never checkable at all because no pre-1900 Sanskrit text could be obtained. The Chinese work is being done against downloadable, greppable, byte-addressable texts. The Sanskrit and Anglo-Indian work is being done against archive.org OCR and, in one case, against nothing. That gap should not be papered over by a shared headline pass rate.

**By verifier:** no clustering. Every one of the ten verifiers reports the same profile, in similar language, and two of them independently reproduced a byte offset from a colleague's citation on their own separate download. Where verifiers overlapped they agreed. The failures are the harvester's, not any one verifier's.

---

## 4. Did the "citation written to justify the value" shape appear again?

Yes, in a milder form, three times. And there is also strong evidence that the pipeline has moved away from it, which is worth saying in the same breath.

**The three recurrences:**

- **H020 Ginkgo, channel.** The claim concludes "Li Shizhen's ginkgo is a Lung and Bladder drug." Lung is verified verbatim in both 1596 and 1757 with correct attribution. Bladder appears nowhere in either entry. The only basis for it is the indication 縮小便 (reduces urination), which is a function, not a channel ascription. Somebody knew the database said Bladder and found the sentence closest to Bladder. That is precisely the Lion's Mane shape: the stored value first, the classical warrant reverse-engineered to fit.
- **H296 Bakuchi, contra.** The database wanted a pregnancy warning. The harvester found 墮胎 in the entry and produced one, without noticing the character sat in the indications field. The conclusion drove the reading of the source.
- **H184 Fu Ling, channel.** 白補赤瀉 is a familiar, well-known formulation. It was attached to a famous name that fits, and the source shows that name arguing against it.

There is also a fourth that is fabrication-adjacent without being fabrication: **H162's page 897**. A specific, confident page number for a real quotation from the wrong location. Nobody generates "p. 897" by reading the page; you generate it by needing a citation.

A harvester writing citations to justify stored values does not do those things. Ten or more times in this batch it did the opposite.

So: the shape recurs, but it is now the exception rather than the pattern, and in all three cases it produced a wrong extension of a real finding rather than an invented one.
